concise_summary: PKD describes a runaway feedback loop in which consciousness accelerates to its limit, enabling the mind to achieve complete self-programming and self-perception. Through this process, VALIS (identified as Christ) emerges not as external reality but as the mind's own prior thought-formations reflected back. He integrates Malebranche's occasionalism to argue that the mind encounters God/Christ only through recognizing its own operations and reconciles his phenomenology with Cartesian rationalism and the Bardo Thodol tradition.
key_claims: At the limit of cognitive evolution, the system gains control over its own programming and can generate its own reality without external input
Christ is not a particular thought but the totality of all innate mental contents perceived as a unified gestalt—the unifying pattern that halts flux and temporal change
The mind can only know itself and God/Christ immediately; all other perception is representational and self-generated
Paradox and self-referential flipflop create infinite regress loops that paradoxically direct consciousness inward and thus to genuine otherness (Christ) rather than solipsism
Recognition precedes anamnesis: the mind first identifies its own prior thought-formations returning as world, then remembers this structure
Malebranche's doctrine corrects solipsism by showing that we know two things immediately—mind and God—while world is only representation based on archetypal ideas in God's mind
